system_prompt_style.evidence_quote:
injecting a source-tagged
`<retrieved-context>` block into the very same turn
system_prompt_style.note: Skills, memory and proactive retrieval appear to be injected at runtime. The system prompt builder (provider/anthropic/prompt.cpp) is in the file tree but its contents are not in the evidence.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote:
Beyond the explicit tool, a **proactive path** runs the funnel *before you ask*
when your message looks knowledge-shaped
env_context_strategy.note: Proactive retrieval is hybrid BM25 plus embeddings (BM25 only when no Ollama server is reachable). The model can also navigate with grep, glob, read and repo_map tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote:
applies a **per-tool output budget** so a runaway `read`/`bash`/`grep`
can't blow the context window
context_compaction.note: Summary compaction fires at 95% of the context window (ARCHITECTURE.md Sec. 8.5).

observation_format.evidence_quote: Tools are fully typed internally; only the dispatcher boundary speaks JSON.
observation_format.note: The code that converts observations to message content is not in the evidence.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote:
`wire::could_be_tool_json` (the leaked-tool-call
prefix sniffer weak local models need)
tool_call_format.note: Native tools are presumed to be the default. The JSON-in-text value comes from the salvage path for weak local models.

tool_count.note: ARCHITECTURE.md lists about 35 shipped tools, but the evidence does not show which tools are exposed to the model by default.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: read · write · edit · bash · grep · glob · git · web · search_docs · search_code · task
edit_primitive.note: The arguments of the edit tool are not shown. The mapping of edit to search_replace and write to whole-file rewrite is inferred from the tool names.

protocol_standardization.note: The other protocol is ACP (Agent Client Protocol). MCP is configured via .agentty/mcp.json.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
A turn is not a single request — it cycles `Streaming → AwaitingPermission →
ExecutingTool → Streaming → … → Idle`.
loop_primitives.note: The runtime is an Elm-style Msg loop. Smart Mode (off by default) adds an escalating cascade.

planning_granularity.note: The README binds a Plan / todo view to the ^T key.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: **Off is a strict byte-for-byte no-op** — zero extra tokens, zero latency.
multi_agent_topology.note: Smart Mode offers an orchestrator-workers topology, but it is off by default. The task subagent tool also exists.

delegation_mechanism.note: The task tool appears to be in the default tool suite.

human_in_loop.note: The Write, Ask and Minimal profiles are selectable. The default profile is not shown.

short_term_state.evidence_quote:
`domain/session.hpp` models this as a
phase variant

long_term_memory.note: Retrieval indexes can also use embeddings, and Smart Mode keeps routing memory in .agentty/.

state_persistence.note: Threads are persisted and reloaded via load_thread.

self_verification.note: The evidence shows no harness-enforced verification. The quote is weak for absence; there is a diagnostics/test tool and a Smart Mode cascade, neither shown to be harness-enforced.

retry_policy.evidence_quote:
a
**cascade** retries at higher effort only when a cheap attempt actually falls
short
retry_policy.note: The Smart Mode cascade (adaptive) is off by default. Stream-level retries are transport retries, not task retries.

rollback.note: workspace/checkpoint.hpp exists in the file tree.

termination_condition.note: No step or cost cap is shown in the evidence.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: the repeated conversation prefix is a prompt-cache HIT across turns
cost_controls.note: Model routing comes from Smart Mode, which is off by default.

timeouts.evidence_quote:
A 120-s stall watchdog trips the
cancel token
timeouts.note: The quoted watchdog is a stream stall timer, not a tool timeout. A per-tool timeout is not shown, so this value is inferred.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Every shell call runs inside bwrap (Linux) / sandbox-exec (macOS).
execution_isolation.note: The sandbox is bwrap or sandbox-exec. This is closest to subprocess-level isolation with an OS sandbox.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: File tools refuse paths outside your workspace.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Run on a box with no internet.
network_policy.note: The optional airgap mode has no internet on the host. Network access is otherwise presumably open.

permission_model.note: The profile-by-effects matrix could also be read as a static rule table.

tracing.evidence_quote: `AGENTTY_ACP_TRACE=1 agentty acp` dumps every JSON-RPC frame to stderr

guardrails.evidence_quote: Shell and build commands run in a sandbox

target_domain.evidence_quote: A blazing-fast, open-source coding agent in your terminal.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Claude, GPT, Groq, OpenRouter, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
